newsitem.title: USA: Colgate earnings up 18 percent to record high.
newsitem.headline: Colgate earnings up 18 percent to record high.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co., the global consumer products giant, said Wednesday its first-quarter earnings jumped 18 percent to a record high, despite the dampening effect of a strong dollar on overseas sales.

The maker of Palmolive soap, Ajax detergent and Hill's Pet foods reported earnings of $169.6 million, or $1.12 a share, vs. earnings of $143.5 million, or 95 cents, in last year's first quarter. Sales edged up to $2.14 billion from $2.05 billion.
Colgate said its North American sales were up 7 percent, while Latin American sales rose 10 percent, boosted by stronger worldwide advertising.

"The simultaneous increase in both advertising and profitability was made possible by a sharp increase in gross profit together with a reduction in the worldwide overhead ratio," Chairman Reuben Mark said.
In Europe, Colgate's sales were off 6 percent due to the impact of currency translation, Colgate said. In Asia and Africa, sales rose 3 percent.
Colgate-Palmolive's stock was up $1.50 at $106.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
